source_title: Sir Patrick Stewart dies at 86: Star Trek and X-Men star passes away at his home in Los Angeles after battle with Alzheimer’s and Lewy body dementia
source_excerpt: Sir Patrick Stewart, the acclaimed British actor celebrated for his performances on stage and his iconic roles in Star Trek: The Next Generation and the X-Men franchise, has died at the age of 86. The actor passed away at his home in Los Angeles on October 28, 2026, following a battle with Alzheimerâs disease and Lewy body dementia.A statement shared on Instagram on Thursday, October 29, announced his death, saying he had been surrounded by his family and friends during his final hours.âWe announce with great sorrow the passing of Sir Patrick Stewart yesterday at his home in Los Angeles, in the loving care of his beloved wife Sunny, following a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimerâs Disease and Lewy Body Dementia,â the statement read.âHe has been held in the warm embrace of family and friends, surrounded by live music, prayer, tears, laughter, and the kind of profound emotion that only he could inspire after a lifetime of devotion to us all,â it continued. âWe will forever cherish the peaceful ease and reflection of his invincible grace.âThe family has requested that, instead of flowers, memorial contributions be made to the Johns Hopkins Alzheimerâs Disease Research Center Fund and the Alzheimerâs Foundation of Americaâs caregiver resources.Sir Patrick Stewartâs six-decade career in theatre and cinemaStewart leaves behind a remarkable career spanning more than six decades, establishing himself as one of Britainâs most distinguished stage and screen actors. His accolades included two Olivier Awards and a Grammy Award, alongside nominations for a Tony Award, three Golden Globes, four Emmy Awards and three Screen Actors Guild Awards.In 2010, Queen Elizabeth II knighted him for his services to drama, recognising his contribution to British theatre and international entertainment.His professional career gained momentum in 1966 when he joined the Royal Shakespeare Company. Although international audiences would eventually associate him with science fiction and superhero films, theatre remained a constant throughout his life.From Captain Jean-Luc Picard to Professor Charles XavierStewart became a global star in 1987 when he was cast as Captain Jean-Luc Picard in Star Trek: The Next Generation. His portrayal of the thoughtful, principled starship captain became one of the defining performances of the franchise.The series ran until 1994, and Stewart subsequently reprised Picard in several Star Trek films, including Star Trek: Generations, Star Trek: First Contact, Star Trek: Insurrection and Star Trek: Nemesis. He returned to the role decades later in Star Trek: Picard, which followed the character in his later years.He reached another generation of moviegoers through the X-Men franchise, playing Professor Charles Xavier, the powerful telepath and mentor to a group of mutants.
